deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E, F, G are complex Hilbert spaces, with compact operators u and w composable as uw. ρ_i(T) denotes the i-th singular value of T, i.e. the i-th eigenvalue of (T*T)^{1/2} in decreasing order. Λ̄^m is the (completed) m-th exterior power, defined on the previous page.

The claim (24) is the multiplicative majorization
 ρ_1(uw)···ρ_m(uw) ≤ (ρ_1(u)ρ_1(w))···(ρ_m(u)ρ_m(w)) for every m.

Proof as sketched on the page:
- For m=1, ρ_1(T) = ||(T*T)^{1/2}|| = ||T||, so the claim is just ||uw|| ≤ ||u|| ||w||.
- For general m, use ρ_i(T)^2 = λ_i(T*T) = λ_i(TT*).
- Then (ρ_1(uw)···ρ_m(uw))^2 = λ_1(TT*)···λ_m(TT*) = λ_1(Λ̄^m(TT*)), with T = uw. The top eigenvalue of the m-th exterior power of a positive operator is the product of its m largest eigenvalues.
- Hence ∏_{i≤m} ρ_i(T) = ||Λ̄^m T||. This identity is the content of (22)/(23) on the previous page.
- Functoriality gives Λ̄^m(uw) = Λ̄^m u · Λ̄^m w.
- So ||Λ̄^m(uw)|| ≤ ||Λ̄^m u|| ||Λ̄^m w|| = ∏ρ_i(u) · ∏ρ_i(w).

Grothendieck notes that the idea behind (23) (Weyl's inequality |λ_1···λ_m| ≤ ρ_1···ρ_m) and (24) seems due to H. Weyl. He adds that Weyl also used them to derive the convexity inequalities of the next §. The next page (§5) applies exterior powers to Fredholm determinants: α_n(u) = Tr Λ̂^n u, |det(1+u)| ≤ det(1+|u|), and Lidskii-type formulas for trace-class u.

Purpose: these estimates are preparatory material for Grothendieck's Fredholm theory in Hilbert/Banach spaces (eigenvalue estimates for nuclear and p-summing operators).
errors: Composition/notation is muddled: the hypothesis line reads like u: E→F and w: F→G, yet the product is written uw. Consistent composition order requires w: E→F and u: F→G (or else the product should be wu). This is harmless for the inequality.
Inside the crossed-out block the squared product is written via eigenvalues of (uw)(uw)*. This is correct because T*T and TT* have the same nonzero eigenvalues, but the page does not justify it.

Exterior powers of a product are used without stating the needed facts: functoriality Λ^m(uw) = Λ^m u Λ^m w, and that the norm of Λ^m T equals the product of the top m singular values. Presumably these are taken from (22)/(23) on the previous page.

ideas.what: Multiplicative majorization of singular values of a product of compact operators, ∏_{i≤m} s_i(uw) ≤ ∏_{i≤m} s_i(u)s_i(w), proved via exterior powers
ideas.modern_name: Horn's inequality (singular values of products) / Gelfand–Naimark–Horn majorization
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Horn (1950); the exterior-power technique is from H. Weyl (1949). Grothendieck attributes the idea to Weyl.
ideas.where_published: Plausibly in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and/or 'Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires' (Mem. AMS 1955), Ch. II on Fredholm determinants and eigenvalue estimates.

ideas.what: The norm of the m-th exterior power of T equals the product of T's top m singular values (from (22)/(23) on the previous page)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct proof of Horn's singular-value product inequality by Weyl's exterior-power method. Grothendieck himself explicitly credits the idea to Weyl. It is standard textbook material (Gohberg–Krein, Simon) and preparatory for his published Fredholm theory, so nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: 'w = uv' in line 2 is likely a mis-reading. The struck text appears to be 'posons ...' and the operators are u and w with product uw.

The line after (24) beginning 'En effet' is the start of a large struck-out (looped) block. Its content runs: c'est évident pour m=1, car on a les formules ρ_1(w)=||(w*w)^{1/2}||=||w||, et la formule se réduit alors à ||uw|| ≤ ||u|| ||w||.
'λ_1(\bar\Lambda^m(uw)(uw)^*)' should read λ_1(Λ̄^m((uw)(uw)^*)); the final '= λ_1' is struck.

The unstruck text after the box reads roughly: 'En effet, en vertu de (23), le premier membre est égal à ||Λ̄^m(uw)||, i.e. ||Λ̄^m u Λ̄^m w||, donc majoré par ||Λ̄^m u|| ||Λ̄^m w||, ce qui achève la démonstration de (24), compte tenu de (23).'
The last line is likely 'leur utilisation pour les inégalités de convexité du § suivant'.
